_comment: Class index -> disease metadata used by the inference service

Healthy Leaf: Continue current irrigation and fertiliser schedule
Scout the field weekly for early symptoms
Maintain weed control to reduce humidity around plants
Leaf Blight: Remove and burn affected leaves immediately
Spray copper-based fungicide (e.g. copper oxychloride) every 7-10 days
Improve airflow by widening plant spacing
Avoid overhead watering; irrigate at soil level
Leaf Rust: Apply triazole fungicide at first sign of orange pustules
Repeat spray after 14 days if pustules persist
Collect and destroy fallen infected leaves
Rotate crops next season to break the disease cycle
Powdery Mildew: Spray wettable sulphur or potassium bicarbonate solution
Water early in the morning so leaves dry quickly
Prune dense canopy to increase sunlight penetration
Bacterial Spot: Remove infected plant material - do not compost
Disinfect tools and wash hands between plants
Use certified disease-free seed for the next planting
Nitrogen Deficiency: Top-dress with urea (46% N) at recommended field rate
Mix compost or well-rotted cattle manure into topsoil
Re-scan leaves in 10 days after treatment

advice.Healthy Leaf: Crop looks healthy. Keep monitoring weekly.
advice.Leaf Blight: High risk of spread. Act within 48 hours.
advice.Leaf Rust: Moderate risk. Treat this week and rescan after spraying.
advice.Powdery Mildew: Moderate risk. Improve airflow and treat promptly.
advice.Bacterial Spot: High risk - quarantine affected plants and treat now.
advice.Nitrogen Deficiency: Nutrition issue, not disease. Fertilise and rescan.
